<details><summary><code>client.<a href="src/fern/client.py">verify_multi_factor</a>(...)</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Completes a pending sign-in with an authenticator or recovery code.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```python
from fern import FernApi

client = FernApi(
    token="<token>",
    base_url="https://yourhost.com/path/to/api",
)

client.verify_multi_factor(
    challenge_token="challengeToken",
    code="code",
)

```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**challenge_token:** `str` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**code:** `str` — An authenticator code or a recovery code. The server decides which by shape; six digits are never matched against recovery codes.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request_options:** `typing.Optional[RequestOptions]` — Request-specific configuration.
    
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

</dl>

<details><summary><code>client.<a href="src/fern/client.py">passkey_login</a>(...)</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Posts the raw WebAuthn assertion. A verified passkey satisfies multi-factor authentication on its own.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```python
from fern import FernApi, WebAuthnAssertionType, WebAuthnAssertionResponse

client = FernApi(
    token="<token>",
    base_url="https://yourhost.com/path/to/api",
)

client.passkey_login(
    mfa_challenge="X-MFA-Challenge",
    id="id",
    raw_id="rawId",
    type=WebAuthnAssertionType.PUBLIC_KEY,
    response=WebAuthnAssertionResponse(
        client_data_json="clientDataJSON",
        authenticator_data="authenticatorData",
        signature="signature",
    ),
)

```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**mfa_challenge:** `str` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**id:** `str` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**raw_id:** `str` — base64url
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**type:** `WebAuthnAssertionType` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**response:** `WebAuthnAssertionResponse` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**authenticator_attachment:** `typing.Optional[WebAuthnAssertionAuthenticatorAttachment]` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**client_extension_results:** `typing.Optional[typing.Dict[str, typing.Any]]` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request_options:** `typing.Optional[RequestOptions]` — Request-specific configuration.
    
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

<details><summary><code>client.<a href="src/fern/client.py">register_passkey</a>(...)</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

The passkey is named from the authenticator's AAGUID; no name is accepted here. Use the rename endpoint to change it.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```python
from fern import FernApi, WebAuthnCredentialType, WebAuthnCredentialResponse

client = FernApi(
    token="<token>",
    base_url="https://yourhost.com/path/to/api",
)

client.register_passkey(
    csrf_token="X-CSRF-Token",
    mfa_challenge="X-MFA-Challenge",
    id="id",
    raw_id="rawId",
    type=WebAuthnCredentialType.PUBLIC_KEY,
    response=WebAuthnCredentialResponse(
        client_data_json="clientDataJSON",
        attestation_object="attestationObject",
    ),
)

```

<details><summary><code>client.<a href="src/fern/client.py">player_heartbeat</a>(...)</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Accepts the authenticated Player heartbeat. Optional Linux Display Control fields report detected providers, independent capabilities, display power observations, and policy state. They do not determine Player online status; command acknowledgement and display state confirmation remain separate.

The optional `noiseMeter` object carries the Noise Meter plugin's live state and its completed ten-second history buckets. It is derived numbers only — no audio, waveform, or sample is exchanged in either direction. The screen is taken from the authenticated device credential, never from the body, and a batch is bounded to 120 records. Storage is idempotent on screen plus bucket start, so a retried heartbeat cannot duplicate history.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```python
from fern import FernApi

client = FernApi(
    token="<token>",
    base_url="https://yourhost.com/path/to/api",
)

client.player_heartbeat()

```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**player_family:** `typing.Optional[str]` — `android`, `electron-linux` or `edge`. The server keeps only these values; another value is recorded as absent.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**player_architecture:** `typing.Optional[str]` — `x86_64` or `aarch64`, kept only with `playerFamily: edge`. An Edge screen without a known architecture is `incompatible` for Edge deployments.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**noise_meter:** `typing.Optional[PlayerHeartbeatNoiseMeter]` — Noise Meter plugin state. Contains no audio, waveform, or sample, and levels are the relative 0-100 Tilecast scale rather than dB, dBA, or SPL.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request_options:** `typing.Optional[RequestOptions]` — Request-specific configuration.
    
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

```python
    },
)
```

<details><summary><code>client.<a href="src/fern/client.py">transition_form_record</a>(...)</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Moves a record to a new workflow state, enforcing the configured transition, per-form capability and record ownership, optimistic concurrency (version), and required-field completeness (including required images, satisfied only by a bound attachment) before any submit transition or any transition into an output-eligible state. A note is recorded as a comment; a transition that requires a note (the default changes_requested path, derived from the workflow) is rejected with 422 when the note is empty. A 409 means the record changed; reload, preserving any unsent note.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```python
from fern import FernApi

)

client.transition_form_record(
    id="id",
    record_id="recordId",
)
```

<details><summary><code>client.<a href="src/fern/client.py">upload_form_record_attachment</a>(...)</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Uploads a base64-encoded image as a dedicated form attachment bound to an image field, returning the updated record detail with its incremented version. Uses optimistic concurrency — the request body must carry the record's current `version`, and a mismatch returns 409. Because image fields are single-valued, uploading to a field that already has an attachment replaces it. Authorization matches record editing. Form attachments are never exposed through the general Media library.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```python
from fern import FernApi

client = FernApi(
    token="<token>",
    base_url="https://yourhost.com/path/to/api",
)

client.upload_form_record_attachment(
    id="id",
    record_id="recordId",
    field_key="fieldKey",
    data="data",
    version=1,
)

```

</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

The selected assigned Linux player joins and leaves the network without starting AirPlay. The durable command contains only the network ID and timeout; credentials are fetched separately by the authenticated player.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```python
from fern import FernApi

client = FernApi(
    token="<token>",
    base_url="https://yourhost.com/path/to/api",
)
```

<details><summary><code>client.<a href="src/fern/client.py">upload_and_verify_a_signed_tilecast_player_release_bundle</a>(...) -> PostApiV1PlayerReleasesUploadResponse</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Accepts one release's three files as multipart files: the artifact, the signed update manifest and its signature. The file names select the family: `tilecast-player.apk` with `tilecast-player-update.json` (Android), `tilecast-player.AppImage` with `tilecast-player-update-linux.json` (Electron Linux), or `tilecast-edge-<version>-<arch>.tar.zst` with the signed envelope `tilecast-edge-update.json` (Tilecast Edge). Owner session plus CSRF or a configured release-publishing bearer token is required.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```python
from fern import FernApi

client = FernApi(
    token="<token>",
    base_url="https://yourhost.com/path/to/api",
)

client.upload_and_verify_a_signed_tilecast_player_release_bundle(
    files=["example_files"],
)

```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**files:** `typing.List[core.File]` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request_options:** `typing.Optional[RequestOptions]` — Request-specific configuration.
    
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

<details><summary><code>client.<a href="src/fern/client.py">report_bounded_player_update_preparation_and_installer_status</a>(...)</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```python
from fern import FernApi, PostApiV1PlayerUpdateDeploymentsDeploymentIdStatusRequestState

client = FernApi(
    token="<token>",
    base_url="https://yourhost.com/path/to/api",
)

client.report_bounded_player_update_preparation_and_installer_status(
    deployment_id="deploymentId",
    state=PostApiV1PlayerUpdateDeploymentsDeploymentIdStatusRequestState.DOWNLOADING,
)

```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**deployment_id:** `str` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**state:** `PostApiV1PlayerUpdateDeploymentsDeploymentIdStatusRequestState` — `succeeded` is accepted only for a Tilecast Edge release: it is the screen's explicit confirmation that the provisional release passed its health checks, and the only way an Edge target settles. Other families settle from the heartbeat.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**downloaded_bytes:** `typing.Optional[int]` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**permission_status:** `typing.Optional[str]` 
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**installer_status:** `typing.Optional[str]` — Tilecast Edge sends `provisional` with `reconnecting`, `confirmed` with `succeeded`, and `rolled_back` with a `failed` report of a release that was activated and then rolled back.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**error:** `typing.Optional[str]` — A bounded reason code, never free text from a server response.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request_options:** `typing.Optional[RequestOptions]` — Request-specific configuration.
    
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>
